You can assign a\\\\nhigher value to more recent content, specific file types, or specific data\\\\nsources.\\\\n\\\\nAmazon Q Business automatically boosts specific document attributes, like\\\\ndocument title, when retrieving information from your index to generate end user chat\\\\nresponses. You can use the boosting feature to customize and control boosting, and also\\\\noverride any pre-existing boosts applied by Amazon Q Business.\\\\n\\\\nWhen you use this feature, a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)-generated result is\\\\ngiven a boost during retrieval when the query includes terms that match that field or\\\\nattribute. You specify how much of a boost the document receives when there is a match.\\\\nWhen Amazon Q Business generates responses, it prioritizes the sources that are\\\\nassigned higher rankings.\\\\n\\\\nChoosing to boost document attributes doesn\\'t by itself cause Amazon Q Business\\\\nto include or exclude a document in the chat response. A boosted document attribute is\\\\nonly one of the factors that Amazon Q Business uses to determine the relevance of\\\\na document.\\\\n\\\\n**Note:**\\\\n\\\\nBoosting in Amazon Q Business is only available if you use an Amazon Q native retrie\\\\n\\\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonq/latest/qbusiness-ug/metadata-boosting.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Amazon Q Business simplifies integration of enterprise knowledge bases at scale | Artificial Intelligence\",\"context\":\"### Boosting performance\\\\n\\\\nWhen working with your specific dataset in Amazon Q Business, you can use relevance tuning to enhance the performance and accuracy of search results. This feature allows you to customize how Amazon Q Business prioritizes information within your ingested documents. For example, if your dataset includes product descriptions, customer reviews, and technical specifications, you can use relevance tuning to boost the importance of certain fields. You might choose to prioritize product names in titles, give more weight to recent customer reviews, or emphasize specific technical attributes that are crucial for your business. Does NOT apply to: S3 policies, Athena, Glue/Iceberg outside Redshift, Aurora, RDS, DynamoDB.\\\\n\\\\nServices: redshift, redshift-serverless, redshift-data-api\\\\nTasks: query, debug, optimize\\\\nPersona: developer, data-engineer, database-administrator, data-analyst\\\\nWorkload: data-warehouse, analytics, etl\\\\n*\",\"skill_name\":\"redshift-guide\"}]}}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "62089f61-c76a-4893-9a8e-67f313a5f4e0", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's how to improve retrieval quality in Amazon Q Business, based on current AWS guidance — and one important heads-up: **Amazon Q Business is closing to new customers on July 31, 2026** (AWS is steering new workloads toward Amazon Quick instead), so keep that in mind if you're planning long-term investment here.

**1. Relevance tuning (replaces the older "metadata boosting")**
This is the main lever for answer quality. It lets you assign weights to document attributes so Q Business ranks the most authoritative/relevant sources higher:
- Boost recency (e.g., prioritize newer documents if stale answers are the issue)
- Boost specific attributes like `_document_title`, file type, or a custom field like `services`
- You configure boost levels (`LOW`/`MEDIUM`/`HIGH`) per attribute, either in the console or via a `BoostingOverrideConfiguration` in your index config
- Note: boosting only works with the **native Q Business retriever/index** — not available if you're using an external retriever like Kendra

**2. Check data freshness and sync health**
A common cause of "irrelevant" answers is actually stale data:
- Review each connector's sync schedule and last successful sync run
- Trigger manual syncs if a connector has fallen behind
- If recency matters for your use case, combine this with relevance tuning boosted on a date/recency attribute

**3. Metadata and document attribute quality**
Boosting only helps if your documents have good metadata to boost on — titles, categories, source tags, dates. Garbage-in metadata limits how well tuning can work.

**4. Review which documents are actually being retrieved**
Worth checking the source citations Q Business returns per answer — if it's consistently pulling from the wrong data source or outdated docs, that points to either a sync/ACL issue or a tuning gap rather than a model problem.

Do you want me to check your actual Q Business application's data source sync status and current boosting configuration in your account, or were you looking for general guidance only?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
